verdict.rationale: Simular documents programmatic, UI-less control of Sai. Developers can send tasks from their own code via a REST API, Python SDK, MCP server, or a standalone CLI. The API also streams progress events and answers approval requests, so runs can proceed without a human watching. However, nothing documents CI pipelines, an official headless or non-interactive mode, or exit codes, so the CI part of the story is only implied. Missing for 10: documented CI integration or examples (e.g., GitHub Actions), an explicit headless/non-interactive mode with exit-status semantics, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Developers can drive Sai from their own code or coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) with the Sai API: send a task in plain language, and Sai completes it on a cloud Windows computer.
gives developers, their code and their coding agents the same autonomous computer through a REST API, a Python SDK and an MCP server.
`GET /v1/agents/events` streams progress; `POST /v1/agents/approve` answers an approval request
Standalone simulang CLI, simulang-js, and the /simulang skill in Claude Code.
